# Test fixture: `apply_flattened` of vllm/model_executor/layers/linear.py at vLLM main@1bdc437 (the
# commit the image builds), verbatim, plus the two names it needs. sly/tests/test_linear_carrier_patch_cpu.py
# applies sly/patch_linear_carrier.py to a copy and runs the result on CPU. Re-extract it when the
# pinned vLLM changes this function (the test compares it with the real file when INKLING_VLLM_SRC is set,
# ci/patch_dryrun.sh checks the real anchor).
from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

import torch

from vllm.model_executor.layers.fusion.quant_activation import QuantizedActivation


def apply_flattened(
    fn: Callable[[Any], torch.Tensor], x: torch.Tensor | QuantizedActivation
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Call `fn` on `x` flattened to 2D, if that can be done without a copy.

    Linear methods and kernels may assume 2D activations, but callers such as
    the Transformers modeling backend pass `[batch, seq, hidden]` activations.
    """
    if isinstance(x, QuantizedActivation):
        if len(x.orig_shape) <= 2:
            return fn(x)
        return fn(x.flatten()).view(*x.orig_shape[:-1], -1)
    if x.ndim <= 2 or not x.is_contiguous():
        return fn(x)
    return fn(x.view(-1, x.shape[-1])).view(*x.shape[:-1], -1)
